about: Where a corner spec (corner_<engine>.json) may differ from its separate engine format, answers must match everywhere. Per workload and engine: `ops` = queries whose per-step op counts may differ, `bytes` = queries whose value bytes may differ ("*" = every query); each with its reason. Read by check_meta_vs_formats.py, which also reports a listed query that did not differ.

ops.why: dgraph's date index is GLOBAL (formats/dgraph, not make_index_backend); the corner uses a per-type posting/day index: rows match, index-op counts differ; (predicted before the run): ic1 -- meta GETs every Split props record, dgraph SEEKs its list predicates (email, language); is4 -- meta's anchor read decides the label once and stops at the first candidate that exists; (predicted before the run): meta's chase reads each node once per op call (chains that meet share it), shares one chunk cache over the hops, and lands a Split hop on the first record; the engine reads per (source, hop) and scans; the run's label memo (predicted before the run): an executor optimization the engine formats do not use yet, not a layout difference -- a probe that hit, or a k = 1 hop, tells the rest of the run the vertex's label, so a later read of the same vids probes less than the engine format does

bytes.why: dgraph's global date index stores larger index values than the corner's per-type one (ic11: bytes only, the same op counts); and a Condensed list is ids as delta-uvarints + the entries' columns (codec/lists.h), dgraph's is UidPack + a RowV2 row per entry
a per-edge record holds the edge's columns (codec/columns.h; 0 columns = empty); nebula's holds a RowV2 row

ops.why: (predicted before the run): meta's chase reads each node once per op call (chains that meet share it), shares one chunk cache over the hops, and lands a Split hop on the first record; the engine reads per (source, hop) and scans; the run's label memo (predicted before the run): an executor optimization the engine formats do not use yet, not a layout difference -- a probe that hit, or a k = 1 hop, tells the rest of the run the vertex's label, so a later read of the same vids probes less than the engine format does

meta's chunks are per (etype, dir, vid group), so a Message's Post and Comment entries share one run, where pertype_csr keeps a run per label: a step that names one label reads the other label's entries too on meta. Both stores keep the far-end label, so a hop knows its far end's label and neither probes the wrong run. Measured at sf0.1, 3 params, against the reported store: hasTag out of a Message (ic4, ic6, ic10, ic12), likes into a Message and the Message properties (ic7), replyOf into or out of a Message (ic8, is2, is7), hasCreator out of a Message (ic8, is2, is7)

bytes.why: the two chunk codecs (meta's codec/lists.h, pertype_csr's codec/chunks.h) store the same entries in other bytes: for one, meta codes an owner's first id from its vid group's base (id << 4: 2 B from 8 on), pertype_csr writes it as it is (1 B up to 127). Measured at sf0.1, 3 params: 18 of 19 queries read other value bytes (is4 reads only a Message's properties); the steps under `ops` add to it

ops.why: a near-match by design: meta deletes with a real del_key (dgraph PUTs a tombstone), keys the type in the key (dgraph writes a dgraph.type record) and keeps a per-type index (dgraph's date index is global); its differing cells are listed, not failed

bytes.why: as on reads (the list and per-edge encodings), and the near-match above

ops.why: meta's chunks are per (etype, dir, vid group), so a Message's Post and Comment entries share one run, where pertype_csr keeps a run per label: a step that names one label reads the other label's entries too on meta. Both stores keep the far-end label, so a hop knows its far end's label and neither probes the wrong run. Measured at sf0.1, 3 params, against the reported store: deleting a Person with its edges (the fair delete) removes its entries from the Message-side runs of hasCreator and likes: one shared run per Message group on meta, a run per label on pertype_csr

bytes.why: a write rewrites chunks in the two chunk codecs (meta's codec/lists.h, pertype_csr's codec/chunks.h) store the same entries in other bytes: for one, meta codes an owner's first id from its vid group's base (id << 4: 2 B from 8 on), pertype_csr writes it as it is (1 B up to 127). Measured at sf0.1, 3 params: 12 of 20 queries write other value bytes
